tagline: Four majors, one tiny ball, and a sport that's half networking.
why: Golf is both a pro sport with global superstars and a social and business ritual, especially in Hong Kong where club memberships are status symbols. Pro golf has been through a civil war since Saudi-backed LIV Golf launched in 2022. Even if you don't play, knowing the majors, the big names and a bit of vocabulary makes you fluent at the 19th hole.

essentials.title: How scoring works
essentials.body: Each hole has a 'par', the number of shots a good player should take (3, 4 or 5). A course is usually par 70-72. Fewer shots is better; '-10' means ten under par.

essentials.title: The four majors
essentials.body: The Masters (April, Augusta), the PGA Championship (May), the US Open (June) and The Open Championship (July, in the UK). Majors define careers.

essentials.title: Tournaments last four days
essentials.body: Pro events are 72 holes over Thursday to Sunday, with a 'cut' after day two that sends half the field home.

essentials.title: The PGA Tour vs LIV
essentials.body: In 2022 Saudi-funded LIV Golf lured stars with huge contracts. It split the sport; talks about a merger dragged on and the majors are where both sides meet.

essentials.title: The Ryder Cup
essentials.body: Europe vs the USA every two years, team match play with wild crowds. The most emotional event in golf. Europe won in 2023 and again away in New York in 2025.

essentials.title: Handicaps let everyone play together
essentials.body: Amateurs have a handicap showing roughly how many shots over par they shoot, so players of different abilities can compete.

names.name: Tiger Woods
names.what: 15 majors, the most famous golfer ever, who transformed the sport's popularity and money from 1997.

names.name: Scottie Scheffler
names.what: American world number one who dominated 2024 and won the PGA and The Open in 2025.

names.name: Rory McIlroy
names.what: Northern Irish star who completed the career Grand Slam by winning the 2025 Masters after an 11-year major drought.

names.name: Jon Rahm
names.what: Spanish Masters champion whose 2023 move to LIV shocked the sport.

names.name: Bryson DeChambeau
names.what: Big-hitting American LIV star and YouTube personality; won the 2024 US Open.

names.name: Phil Mickelson
names.what: Six-time major winner and one of LIV's first big signings.

names.name: Augusta National
names.what: The private Georgia club that hosts the Masters, famous for azaleas and secrecy.

names.name: St Andrews
names.what: Scotland's 'home of golf', where the game has been played for 600 years.

names.name: Nelly Korda
names.what: American star of the women's LPGA Tour.

names.name: Hideki Matsuyama
names.what: Japan's first men's major champion, winning the 2021 Masters.

names.name: LIV Golf
names.what: Saudi-backed tour with team events and 54-hole tournaments. It held events in Hong Kong in 2024 and 2025.

timeline.event: Jack Nicklaus wins the Masters at 46.
Tiger Woods wins the Masters by 12 shots at 21.
The 'Tiger Slam': Woods holds all four majors at once.
Tiger wins the Masters again after back surgeries and scandal.
Tiger badly injures his leg in a car crash.
LIV Golf launches and splits the sport.
The PGA Tour and LIV's backer announce a surprise merger plan.
McIlroy completes the career Grand Slam; Europe win the Ryder Cup in New York.

now.headline: Race to Dubai finale
now.detail: At the DP World Tour Championship, Rory McIlroy and Tyrrell Hatton share the lead at -5 after two rounds; the final round is Sunday.

now.headline: Rory chases a record
now.detail: A win would give McIlroy an eighth Race to Dubai title, equalling Colin Montgomerie's record.

now.headline: Rory's 2026 Masters
now.detail: McIlroy won the Masters again in April; the other majors went to Aaron Rai, Wyndham Clark and Ryan Fox.

now.headline: USA win the Presidents Cup
now.detail: The US came back to win 17-13 at Medinah in September, an 11th straight win over the Internationals.

now.headline: Scheffler's FedEx Cup
now.detail: Scottie Scheffler won the Tour Championship and the FedEx Cup in August.

now.headline: Hero World Challenge next
now.detail: Tiger Woods' Bahamas event on 6 December is the next big-name stop.

local.headline: Fanling
local.detail: The Hong Kong Golf Club at Fanling hosts the Hong Kong Open, Asia's oldest national open (since 1959). Part of the course has been taken back by the government for housing, which is controversial.

local.headline: Memberships are huge money
local.detail: Debentures at top Hong Kong clubs cost millions of dollars, making membership a status symbol.

local.headline: Where people actually play
local.detail: The public Jockey Club Kau Sai Chau course in Sai Kung, driving ranges, simulator bars, and weekend trips to Shenzhen, Dongguan and Mission Hills.

local.headline: Business golf
local.detail: Golf weekends in Thailand, Japan or Mission Hills are a classic way to entertain clients.

debates.question: Is LIV good or bad for golf?
debates.sides: Supporters say players deserved more money; critics call it Saudi 'sportswashing' that broke the tour.

debates.question: Tiger or Jack: the greatest?
debates.sides: Jack has 18 majors; Tiger had the highest peak and more total wins.

debates.question: Is golf too slow and exclusive?
debates.sides: Shorter formats and simulators are trying to fix it.

debates.question: Should the ball be rolled back?
debates.sides: Courses are being made obsolete by long drives, but rollbacks frustrate players.
